question: For all positive integers \(n,\) let \(f(n) = \log_{2002} n^2.\) Let \[N = f(11) + f(13) + f(14).\] Which of the following relations is true?
solution:
The useful observation is that \(11\cdot13\cdot14=2002\), the base of the logarithms. Combining the three logarithms therefore produces a power of their base. All arguments are positive, and the base \(2002\) is positive and different from \(1\), so the product rule applies:
\[
\begin{aligned}
N&=\log_{2002}(11^2\cdot13^2\cdot14^2)\\
&=\log_{2002}\bigl((11\cdot13\cdot14)^2\bigr)\\
&=\log_{2002}(2002^2)=2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus D gives the exact value. Since \(2>1\), choice A is also true. As displayed, the question has two true choices, A and D, although D is the intended keyed answer.
